formats.key: multicall((address to, bytes data, uint256 value, bool skipRevert, bytes32 callbackHash)[] bundle)
effects: The signer sends msg.value in native currency to Bundler3; the function is payable and nothing checks that msg.value equals the sum of the inner call values.
Bundler3 stores the signer as the transient `initiator`, so adapters that read `initiator()` can pull the signer's tokens through approvals and authorizations the signer gave them.
For each bundle element, Bundler3 calls `to` with `data` and sends `value` native currency from its own balance; the inner calls decide which assets leave or reach the signer.
When `skipRevert` is true, a failing inner call is ignored and the rest of the bundle runs.
When `callbackHash` is non-zero, the callee is allowed to call `reenter` with one specific bundle, which runs more calls while the signer is still the initiator.
Native currency left over in Bundler3 (msg.value above the inner values) stays in a contract that lets anybody make arbitrary calls, so anybody can take it.
formats.shown: The intent "Bundler3 Multicall" and one 'Action' field per bundle element, decoded as nested calldata for `to` with that element's `value`; msg.value, skipRevert and callbackHash are not shown.

findings.title: multicall is payable but shows no field for msg.value, and the code does not check it against inner values.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol multicall: `function multicall(Call[] calldata bundle) external payable` and nothing compares msg.value to the sum of `bundle[i].value`. Descriptor multicall fields: only `#.bundle.[].data` with `amountPath: #.bundle.[].value`; no `@.value` field.
findings.fix: Add a field `{"path": "@.value", "label": "Total value sent", "format": "amount"}` with visible always. The interpolated intent can mention it.

findings.title: multicall hides skipRevert, so an action shown on screen may fail silently while the rest runs.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol _multicall: `if (!bundle[i].skipRevert && !success) UtilsLib.lowLevelRevert(returnData);`. Descriptor shows only `#.bundle.[].data`; `skipRevert` is not a field.
findings.fix: Add a field for `#.bundle.[].skipRevert` with label "Continue if this action fails", or say in the intent that some actions are optional.

findings.title: multicall nested calls set no spenderPath, though adapters act for the initiator (the signer), not Bundler3.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol multicall: `initiator = msg.sender;` with `@dev Locks the initiator so that the sender can be identified by other contracts.` Descriptor params: `calleePath: #.bundle.[].to`, `amountPath: #.bundle.[].value`, no `spenderPath`. A nested adapter descriptor that uses `@.from` gets Bundler3, while the tokens are pulled from the signer.
findings.fix: Add `"spenderPath": "@.from"` so nested adapter descriptors see the signer as the party whose tokens move.

findings.title: multicall intent "Bundler3 Multicall" does not tell the signer what the bundle does.
findings.evidence: Descriptor multicall: `"intent": "Bundler3 Multicall"`. All asset effects come from the nested calls, and the intent names none of them.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Run Morpho batch of actions". Add an interpolatedIntent if the wallet supports a count or summary of the actions.

findings.title: multicall hides callbackHash, which lets a callee re-enter with a bundle carried inside nested data.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol _multicall: `else reenterHash = keccak256(bytes.concat(bytes20(to), callbackHash));`. The reenter bundle sits inside the inner call data (for example flash-loan callback data). That is a nested array in bytes, which ERC-7730 cannot decode.
findings.fix: No descriptor change shows the re-entered bundle today. It waits on support for nested calldata in callback bytes.

formats.key: reenter((address to, bytes data, uint256 value, bool skipRevert, bytes32 callbackHash)[] bundle)
effects: Runs a further bundle of calls from Bundler3 while the original initiator is still set, so adapters can again move the initiator's tokens.
Each element calls `to` with `data` and `value` from Bundler3's balance; skipRevert lets an inner call fail silently.
Only the last unreturned callee with the matching reenterHash can call it; a signer's top-level transaction always reverts.
formats.shown: The intent "Reenter Bundler3" and one 'Action' field per bundle element, decoded as nested calldata for `to` with that element's `value`.

findings.title: reenter has a format, but no signer calls it directly; a top-level call always reverts.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol reenter: `require(reenterHash == keccak256(bytes.concat(bytes20(msg.sender), keccak256(msg.data[4:]))), ErrorsLib.IncorrectReenterHash());`. reenterHash is transient and is set only inside _multicall, so it is zero at the start of a transaction.
findings.fix: Remove the reenter format, or keep it only for smart accounts that act as the callee in a bundle.

findings.title: reenter hides skipRevert, so an action shown on screen may fail silently while the rest runs.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol _multicall: `if (!bundle[i].skipRevert && !success) UtilsLib.lowLevelRevert(returnData);`. The descriptor reenter format shows only `#.bundle.[].data`.
findings.fix: Add a field for `#.bundle.[].skipRevert` with label "Continue if this action fails".

findings.title: reenter nested calls set no spenderPath, though adapters act for the stored initiator.
findings.evidence: Bundler3.sol: `address public transient initiator;` stays set during reenter. Descriptor reenter params have no `spenderPath`.
findings.fix: Add `"spenderPath"` pointing to the signer so nested adapter descriptors see the right party.

couldNotCheck: The bundle's effects on the signer's tokens happen in the callees, the Morpho adapters (for example GeneralAdapter1), which read Bundler3.initiator. Their source is not in the directory, so I could not check which party the nested descriptors need as @.from.
